title: Reading a Guest's Elections Together under the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan
content:
A guest's Keyturn Guest Protection Plan elections are read together when the marketplace decides what it
will cover them for, even though each election covers a single trip.

Losses settled against the guest are counted across every election they have held over the rolling twelve
months, and where that count reaches the level's suspension threshold the guest may no longer elect that level
until the level's waiting period has run, counted in whole calendar days from the day the last loss was settled.
A guest barred from one level may still elect a lower one, and declining marketplace protection altogether is
always open to a guest who can evidence their own motor policy.

Days already covered in the calendar year are read together as well, and a guest whose covered days would take
one trip past the level's maximum trip length is quoted on the level that will carry the whole trip rather than
on one that would run out midway.

## The two counts the marketplace reads

| The count | What is counted | Over what period |
|---|---|---|
| Losses settled against the guest | Every deductible raised against the guest, across all of their elections | The rolling twelve calendar months counted back from the handling date, that date included |
| Days already covered | The days of cover carried by the guest's protection fee lines | From the first day of the current calendar year to the handling date, that date included |

## Points of judgement

**The suspension threshold and the waiting period are the level's own.** Each level of the Keyturn Guest
Protection Plan records its own count of settled losses at which it closes to the guest and its own waiting
period in calendar days; both are recorded against the level itself.

**A closed level does not close the ladder.** Where a level has closed to a guest, the levels below it remain
open to them, and declining marketplace protection remains open on evidence of the guest's own motor policy.

**The waiting period runs from the settlement, not from the suspension.** It is counted in whole calendar days
from the day the last loss was settled. On a hypothetical waiting period of 90 calendar days beginning with a
loss settled on the first day of a month, the guest stands inside the waiting period on the ninetieth day
counted from that day and outside it on the ninety-first.

**Length is quoted forward, not discovered later.** Where the days the guest has already been covered for in
the calendar year would carry one trip past a level's maximum trip length, the quote is written on a level
that will carry the whole trip rather than on one that would run out midway through it.
